params.message:
A claim is judged against the world after the change, never before it

Two headers proposals were refuted seven minutes after they merged,
against an exposure measurement taken before the merge; one of the two
sites was already sending all three headers at that moment, and the other
had not been deployed yet. Merging is not deploying, and deploying is not
measuring.

The judge now waits for a reading taken after the pull request landed:
no reading since the merge is no verdict, exactly as an open proposal is
no verdict. This was never only a headers problem; every claim type
compared against whatever the last measurement happened to say.

A refutation costs a playbook its rung for good, so judging too early
writes a record that is wrong in the harshest direction.
